answer: Distinct-route time ledger: an identity gains standing only while independent peers observe its network path continuously over time, with small wander in latency tolerated but repeated co-location merging identities. Each probe records a route delta against that identity’s prior path and nearby agents. An attacker must maintain a separate network island with an independent timing history for each sybil, paying ongoing probe-response and route-repair labor per identity; shared infrastructure exposes correlated fingerprints.
